statement: Let n = len(nums) and let D = { |nums[i] - nums[j]| : 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, |i - j| >= x }. The function returns a result r such that r = min(D). Equivalently: (a) for every i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, and |i - j| >= x, we have r <= |nums[i] - nums[j]|; and (b) there exist i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, |i - j| >= x, and |nums[i] - nums[j]| = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: For every nums and x satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, overflow, or panic).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: The returned value r satisfies r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: Let n = len(nums), M = max_{0 <= i < n} nums[i], and m = min_{0 <= i < n} nums[i]. Then r <= M - m.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: The returned value r is 0 if and only if x = 0 or there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, |i - j| >= x, and nums[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: Let n = len(nums). If x = n - 1, then r = |nums[0] - nums[n - 1]|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: There exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, |i - j| >= x, and r = |nums[i] - nums[j]|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: For every i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, and |i - j| >= x, we have r <= |nums[i] - nums[j]|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: If x >= 1 and nums[i] != nums[j] for every pair (i, j) with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, and i != j, then r >= 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.
Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: Let n = len(nums). If x >= 1, then r = min{ |nums[i] - nums[j]| : 0 <= i < j < n and j - i >= x }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and let rev be the array of length n defined by rev[i] = nums[n - 1 - i] for 0 <= i < n. Then the minimum absolute difference for rev with the same x equals r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= x <= n - 1.
